newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Court asked to stop Manila mining liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Court asked to stop Manila mining liberalisation.

text.p: Philippine tribal groups asked the Supreme Court on Friday to void a new law allowing foreign mining firms to own up to 100 percent equity in local mining projects, saying natural resources were the nation's heritage.
Several tribal groups challenged the Mining Law in a class suit filed on their behalf by congressman Wigberto Tanada.

"Natural resources constitute the exclusive heritage of the Filipino nation," they said in their petition. "They should therefore be preserved for those under the sovereign authority of that nation and for their posterity."
The court did not say when it would act on the suit.
President Fidel Ramos signed the mining law in 1995 liberalising the industry as part of his economic reform programme to attract more foreign investors.
The petition also asked the Supreme Court to ban Ramos from signing financial and technical assistance agreements (FTAA) with foreign companies for them to develop new mining areas.
The suit was the latest in a series of legal challenges by various groups to the government's liberalisation policies.

The Supreme Court on Monday voided the sale of historic Manila Hotel to a Malaysian firm which had won the 1995 bidding for the hotel, and ordered it sold to a local company in keeping with the "Filipino First" policy.
An appeals court last week also halted the privatisation of the Manila waterworks system after another group challenged Ramos' authority to privatise it.
The court issued the halt order after two consortia jointly owned by Filipinos and foreigners were declared winners of contracts to run the state firm.
One hundred FTAA applications are pending before the government, covering 8.4 million hectares (20.7 million acres) and 64 of the applications are from foreign firms, the petition added.
The tribesmen also said liberalising the mining industry would dislocate cultural minorities from their "ancestral lands."
The Philippines has so far approved the FTAA applications of Western Mining Corp and Arimco, both of Australia.

The government last year revised the implementing rules of the new mining law to strengthen environmental safeguards after tonnes of waste leaked into a river from a mine run by Marcopper Mining Corp, a unit of Placer Dome Inc.
